subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should unconfigured memory search get a non-zero periodic sync fallback by default, or should the periodic fallback remain opt-in while watcher resilience is repaired separately?
rationale: The bug is real, but changing `intervalMinutes` from disabled to default-on creates background filesystem/hash/provider work for existing users and needs an explicit compatibility choice.

options.title: Default-on fallback after repair
options.body: Accept a non-zero interval fallback once the PR is rebased and the interval dirty/rescan path is scoped to memory-source managers.

options.title: Keep fallback opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at `0`, repair watcher/error handling only, and document `intervalMinutes` as the workaround for users who want periodic safety checks.

options.title: Ask for live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue blocked on a current-main long-running watcher reproduction before changing defaults or fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Default-on fallback after repair
recommendation.body: Accept a non-zero interval fallback once the PR is rebased and the interval dirty/rescan path is scoped to memory-source managers.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a product/config compatibility choice across memory runtime defaults, and this person has the strongest broad memory-core ownership signal in the available history.
